anatomy.flutter: Surface(spec: ShadowStyle, radius, fill, border, child) is a DecoratedBox stack: fill+outer boxShadow on the outer DecoratedBox, an inset-painting CustomPaint (_InsetShadowPainter) layered when spec.hasInset, and the border painted last via a DecoratedBox+Padding wrapper so box-sizing: border-box is preserved.
anatomy.web: No component at all — surface.dart's own doc calls itself the counterpart to a family of CSS custom properties: --shadow-pressed, --shadow-btn, --shadow-btn-primary, --shadow-btn-value, --shadow-btn-down, --shadow-chip, --shadow-key/-key-down in styles/tokens.css lines 440-465, consumed as shadow-* Tailwind utilities directly on a bordered/filled element (e.g. `rounded-lg border border-input bg-card shadow-pressed` in surface/page.tsx's SurfaceSpecimen).

api.flutter: Surface takes spec (a ShadowStyle carrying outer+inset ShadowLayer lists), radius (BorderRadius), fill (Color?), border (BoxBorder?) and child — a paint recipe, not a set of variant enums.
api.web: There is no component API: a caller picks one of the eight shadow-* utility class names (shadow-pressed, shadow-btn, shadow-btn-primary, shadow-btn-value, shadow-btn-down, shadow-chip, shadow-key, shadow-key-down) documented in surface/page.tsx's Classes disclosure block and composes it with ordinary border/bg-* classes.
api.note: This is a real platform difference, not a gap: CSS box-shadow (including inset layers) is a native paint primitive with no Flutter counterpart, so the web expresses the effect as a token+utility pair while Flutter has to synthesize the inset layers with a CustomPainter (_InsetShadowPainter). Both sides converge on the same eight named shadow recipes and the same --rim/--ink-*/--wall tokens; the surface is correctly a CSS class on web and a paint widget in Flutter.

states.flutter: Surface itself is a StatelessWidget with no internal state — it paints whatever spec/fill/border it is handed each frame; state (hover/press/focus) lives in the caller (e.g. Switch, Toggle, Button) that swaps which ShadowStyle it passes in.
states.web: The shadow-* utilities are static box-shadow declarations with no :hover/:focus/:active variants of their own; state-driven shadow swaps (e.g. shadow-btn to shadow-btn-down on :active) are written by the consuming component's own class list, not by this token family.
states.note: Neither side gives Surface/shadow-* its own state matrix — it is a pure paint primitive consumed by stateful controls, so there is nothing for this dimension to compare on either side.

disabled.flutter: Surface has no enabled/disabled parameter at all; a disabled control wraps itself in the separate Disabled widget and still hands Surface whatever fill/spec it wants painted.
disabled.web: The shadow-* classes carry no disabled: variant; disabled styling (opacity, cursor) is applied by the consuming component's own disabled:/data-disabled: classes, as documented in surface/page.tsx's Accessibility note about pairing a shadow change with a border or text change.
disabled.note: A shadow token is not itself a control and has no disabled state to express; both sides correctly leave disabled handling to whatever composes the surface.

interaction.flutter: Surface has no gesture handling, no FocusNode, and no pointer callbacks — build() only paints boxShadow/inset layers/border around child.
interaction.web: The shadow-* utilities carry no interaction wiring; keyboard/pointer handling belongs entirely to whatever element (button, input) the class is applied to.
interaction.note: A shadow effect is not interactive on either platform; the note exists only to satisfy the validator's requirement that a non-match verdict explain itself, and n/a is correct here.

semantics.flutter: Surface wraps no Semantics node of its own — it is purely a paint widget; accessible naming/roles are supplied by whatever caller (Switch, Button) wraps it in its own Semantics.
semantics.web: The shadow-* utilities carry no ARIA attributes; surface/page.tsx's own Accessibility section states the real accessibility requirement is that depth alone must never be the sole signal of interactivity or state change, which is a content-authoring rule rather than a semantics API.
semantics.note: Depth/shadow is decorative in the accessibility tree on both platforms, so there is no accessible-naming or role dimension for a pure paint primitive to carry — both sides correctly push that requirement onto the consuming control.
